name: Desert Drives
about: Dunes, wadis, Hatta trails and stargazing spots within a few hours of Dubai. Route notes, fuel stops and safety first.

stories.author: p04
stories.text: Sunset dune drive near Al Qudra, tyres aired down to 18 psi. Worth every bump.

stories.author: p02
stories.text: Wadi hike at dawn, cold water and a lot of shade under the rocks. Pure bliss.

stories.author: p08
stories.text: Campfire coffee in the desert, a thermos and a stove. My new favourite ritual.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Sunset drive to the Al Qudra dunes this Friday. Meet at the lay-by at 4:30pm, bring water, a first aid kit and a tow strap. Tyres aired down, nobody gets stuck alone.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Count me in. I've got the tow strap and the snacks, Tomasz. Tyres at 18 psi?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: I'll follow in my car and bring extra water. Keep the convoy slow and steady.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Sunset in the dunes with a playlist is my dream Friday. Coming with the speaker, low volume.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll bring the thermos and a stove for the coffee at the top of the dune. Good plan.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Dune driving with a group needs a leader and a spotter. Who's the leader this week?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @omar_q I'll lead, you spot. We swap at the second stop so everyone gets a turn.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy is not allowed in the dunes, sadly. But I'll send him a dune photo to dream about.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Hot tip: reduce tyre pressure slowly and carry a pump to inflate before the highway.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our team has never done dunes. Is it safe for beginners in a normal SUV?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @hannah_b a high-clearance SUV is best. Stay with the group and follow the leader's line.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dune snacks, a pastry box and a chilled drink. The desert is hungry work.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Bring a blanket for the sunset, the sand gets cooler quickly after the sun goes down.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Sunset photos on the dune are the best part. Bring a power bank for the phone.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Please keep the rubbish in the car, the desert is not a bin. Leave no trace.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Absolutely. Pack it in, pack it out, and the desert stays beautiful for everyone.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Check the wind forecast before you go, sand storms are not fun. Good luck all.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good point, Omar. I'll check the forecast tomorrow and post it in the thread.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Sunset at 6:20pm, so leave the dunes by 7:15 to be safe. Better to be early.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks everyone, I'll join the convoy and watch and learn. Yalla, desert.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Going to be an amazing evening. See you all at the lay-by, Tomasz.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Desert sunsets are the best free show in the country. Let's go.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy sends his regards from the balcony, with a very long sigh.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Yalla, convoy on Friday. Send photos, the sand looks amazing from the top 🌅

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee at the top of the dune, the best place in the city. See you Friday.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Safe driving and a great sunset, everyone. Remember to keep the speed low.

posts.author: p02
posts.text: Wadi hike in Hatta at dawn: 6km loop, two small waterfalls in the rainy season and a lot of shade under the rocks. Water is essential, even in the cool morning.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Wadi hikes at dawn are the best. The rocks are cool and the light is beautiful.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Water is the most important item. Carry two litres per person, even for a short loop.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee at the top of the wadi is my reward. Bring a flask, nothing else needed.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dawn hike and then a pastry at the bottom of the wadi. A perfect Saturday for me.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would love the wadi, but I'll check if dogs are allowed on the trail first.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good shoes with grip for the rocks. Trail runners are my best friend on the wadi.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: The waterfalls in the rainy season are magical. Check the weather before you go.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Hatta trail maps are in the visitor centre, pick one up if you can. Very useful.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our team wants a wadi hike next month. Any beginner-friendly loops you recommend?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: @hannah_b the 4km loop near the dam is perfect for beginners, with clear signs.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Carry a small first aid kit and a phone with offline maps. The signal can be patchy.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good point. Share your route with a friend before you head out, always.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I like the quiet of the wadi at dawn, no traffic, just birds and the wind.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dawn wadi, lovely. Bring a light snack for the top, a cake is too heavy for the rocks.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy vote for the wadi: yes, if the trail allows dogs, and he has his own water.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A hot day on the wadi is punishing. Start early and finish before the noon heat.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Music is not allowed on some trails, respect the quiet of the nature, friends.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Stay on the marked path, the rocks can be slippery after the rain. Be careful.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thanks everyone, this is a great list of tips. I'll bring the trail runners.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: The wadi hike is on my list now. The team will be so happy to see the waterfalls.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck, Hannah. Take photos of the rock patterns, they're gorgeous.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Enjoy the wadi, everyone. Water, shade and good company. Yalla!

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee and wadi, my new favourite combo. Thank you Ravi for the route.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A wadi hike with a pastry at the bottom. The best way to end a dawn walk.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: The desert sky after a wadi hike is a lovely reward. Go explore 🌄

posts.author: p08
posts.text: Campfire coffee in the desert: a stove, a small kettle, and a moka pot for the bold. Smell of smoke, stars overhead, no traffic. Who wants to try a night at the camp?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Campfire coffee is the best coffee. I'm in for the night at the camp, with the bike too.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Moka pot over a fire? I want to see that. Bring the playlist and the blanket.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Stars over the desert are unmatched. Bring a warm jacket, the nights are cold.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Sunrise run from the camp, the sand is firm at dawn. Count me in for that.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll bring cake for the campfire, a sweet end to the evening. Pastry in the dunes.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy can't come to the dunes, but he would love the campfire smell, I'm sure.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Fire safety is key. Check the rules for campfires, and keep water next to it.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Make sure the fire is out before you sleep, the desert wind can spread sparks fast.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: We have never done camping in the desert. Is there a campsite that allows tents?

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @hannah_b yes, a few licensed camps near the dunes. Book ahead, they fill up in winter.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dune camp with a tent and a sunrise coffee, the perfect easy adventure.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Stars, music, and a moka pot, Yusuf. You're turning the desert into a cafe.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Pack a headlamp, not just a phone. Red light keeps the night vision nice.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Early morning run from camp, cool sand, and a great view. The best way to wake up.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Swim in the desert? Ha, no, but a dip in a nearby pool after the hike is great.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Hot chocolate by the fire, marshmallows, the cosy desert night. Sold.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: I'll bring the warm blankets and the good lamp. Desert nights are colder than you think.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's rule for camping: a soft blanket and a warm lap. He's very adaptable.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's book the camp for next month. I'll gather the team and send the details.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Thanks everyone. The campfire coffee is waiting, and so is the moka pot.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good luck, Hannah. Camp life is the best team bonding in the desert.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Camping plus runs plus coffee, my holy trinity in the desert. Let's go.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Yalla, campfire night. Bring stories, songs and the bold coffee.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Stars, coffee and friends, a perfect desert night. I'm in.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dessert under the stars, can't wait. Yusuf, bring the moka!

posts.author: p07
posts.text: Beginner question: is it okay to drive a normal car to the lookout point near the dunes, or do I really need a 4x4? I want to see the view without damaging the car.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: The lookout point is on the paved road, a normal car is fine. Dunes need a 4x4.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Stick to the marked roads, and don't drive on the soft sand with a normal car.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Normal car is fine, but check the tyres and the fuel before you leave the city.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Petrol stations are few on the desert roads. Fill up before you go, always.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: I've seen people get stuck in the soft sand with a sedan. Don't be that person.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Lookout point with a picnic and cake, nice for a normal car day. Good choice, Anjali.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would love the view but not the dunes. The lookout point is a good compromise.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Bring water and a phone charger. The lookout is quiet, so keep the music low.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks, Anjali. Going to the lookout first before deciding on the dune trip.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: @hannah_b the lookout is a great first step. You'll learn the road before the dunes.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Check the road closures before you go, some sections get closed in bad weather.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good advice, Tomasz. A quick check of the official road status saves a lot of trouble.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Look at the map the night before, and set the route offline. Simple, safe, and calm.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee at the lookout with a thermos, the view and the flask make a great pair.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: The lookout at sunset is my favourite. Pack a blanket and a playlist.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Lookout cake, the new trend. Let's make it a Desert Drives tradition.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's lookout photo is ready, he looked very serious about the view.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Anjali, thanks for asking. These answers are a great starter guide for newcomers.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Starter guide, yes. Let's pin a list of car types and the routes they can take.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good idea. I'll add my dune and road notes in the pinned post this week.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep it simple: normal car for the lookout, 4x4 for the dunes, and always a buddy.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Simple rules are the best. Thanks all, the lookout trip is on for this weekend.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thank you all, this is so helpful. I'll post photos from the lookout on Sunday.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Looking forward to the photos, Anjali. Yalla, the desert is calling 🏜️

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Lookout views are best just before sunset. Plan the timing and bring a jacket.

posts.author: p01
posts.text: Lost my phone signal for six hours on a desert drive and it was the best digital detox I've had. Paper map, a thermos and a good book. Highly recommend.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Digital detox in the desert is the best. Coffee and a book, the perfect pairing.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Six hours without messages is the dream. Pastry, coffee and silence, pure heaven.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Offline maps saved me once. Download the area before you leave, it's a must.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Silence in the desert is a good reset. Also a good reason to tell people your plan.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: No signal means no running app, which is a shame, but the view makes up for it.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would be bored without his phone, but he would love the peace and quiet.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Paper maps are underrated. Bring one, and a compass, in case the battery dies.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: I'll try the detox on the next trip. Maybe two hours first, to be brave.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our team needs this. We'll try a no-phone hour at the camp, maybe that's a start.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: @hannah_b a phone-free hour is a great start. You'll be surprised how calm it feels.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Carry a satellite messenger if you do long desert drives, it's a safety net.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good call, Tomasz. Safety first, detox second. Let people know the route.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A thermos, a paper map and a notebook, that's my desert kit. No screens needed.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Notebook for pastry recipes in the desert, yes! I'll bring one too.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's favourite detox is a long nap in the shade. Very effective, very relaxing.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Desert quiet is great for thinking. I always get my best ideas on a long drive.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: No notifications for six hours, the best gift for the mind. Thanks for sharing, Sara.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Digital detox is my new goal for the summer. One desert day, then a month of balance.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Anjali, the month of balance plan is a great idea. Let's do it as a group.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Group detox challenge in the desert, a fun team goal. Count me in.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the detox safe and sensible. Good signal is great, no signal is also fine.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee plus silence is the ultimate desert combo. Thanks for the reminder, Sara.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: I'll try the paper map and the book this weekend, a very cosy plan.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Enjoy the silence, friends, and bring water. The desert is calm but not forgiving.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves the desert detox. He is already dozing in the sun on the balcony.

posts.author: p04
posts.text: Fuel and rest stop map for the desert roads, updated this week. Petrol stations are far apart, so plan your stops and keep an eye on the gauge. Map link in the group.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Thank you, Tomasz. Fuel stops are the most important part of a desert plan.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the rest stop toilets in mind too, they are sometimes far apart. Plan ahead.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: A coffee stop on the map would be a nice addition, Tomasz. Even a flask stop counts.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: This map is very useful for newcomers. Save it to your phone before you leave.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Fuel at half a tank is my rule in the desert. Never go below that line.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Rest stops with shade and water are my favourite. The desert heat is serious.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy needs water at the rest stops, so this map is a lifesaver for us.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Map is clear and easy to read. Thank you, Tomasz, for the hard work.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: I'll share the map with the team, and we'll plan our trip around the stops.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: @hannah_b good, share it with the team. Keep the map updated after each trip too.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Mark the stops with the best views too, runners like a good view at a rest stop.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Good idea, Ravi. Add a note on the shade and water at each stop.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Tomasz, the coffee stop near the highway exit is worth adding. Ask for the strong brew.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Pastry stop on the map is my request. A cake for the road, please.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's rest stop is the one with the water bowl, mark it in red, please.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thank you all for the ideas. The map is becoming a community project.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Community maps are the best kind. Keep adding, friends, and keep it honest.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Yes, honest and updated. The desert roads change, so check before you leave.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Thanks everyone. I'll print a copy for the glovebox, just in case.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Glovebox copy is a smart move. Batteries die, paper doesn't.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Good luck with the trips, everyone. Water, fuel and a plan, always.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Stay safe and enjoy the open road. The desert is beautiful when you respect it.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Thanks for the map, Tomasz. Coffee and fuel, a good road trip combo ☕

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Map is saved, cake is packed, and the desert is calling. Yalla 🏜️

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thanks, Tomasz. A list of petrol stations with opening hours would be a great next step.

posts.author: p10
posts.text: Dune driving safety basics: lower tyre pressure gradually, never stop on a slope, keep a steady speed, and always stay in a convoy. Yes, this is the boring post. Please read it.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Boring but essential, Omar. The stop on the slope rule saved us once. Read it, everyone.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Steady speed is the hardest rule for me, I always want to go faster. Thanks for the reminder.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Convoy rules are the best safety net. Never go alone in the dunes, that's the golden rule.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Tyre pressure gradually, yes. Quick deflation is the way people get into trouble.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'd add: carry a shovel and a board, not just a strap. The sand is stubborn.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Boring posts are the most useful ones. Thank you, Omar, for the careful advice.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's safety rule: always stay with the group, even on the walks. Same principle.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Keep your speed steady and your eyes forward. The dune crests hide the drop.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our team will read this before the first trip. Thanks for making it simple.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: @hannah_b read it twice, and do a training run on flat sand first. Good practice.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Flat sand practice is great for learning the feel of the car. Start slow.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A pump in the car is essential. Re-inflating before the highway is the step people skip.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Please also check the coolant and the oil before a long desert trip. Heat is hard on engines.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Good reminder. A quick check at the petrol station is a small price for safety.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Leave a note with the route and return time at home. It's a simple thing that matters.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A note at home, a cake in the car, and a happy heart. The essentials.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the safety rules. He always stays close to the leash.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thank you Omar, I've bookmarked this post. Safety is the best adventure.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Adding these rules to the team travel policy. Thank you for the clear list.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Great to see the group taking safety seriously. The desert deserves respect.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Keep it safe, friends. The dunes are the best place to learn patience.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Thanks all. Drive safe, stay in the convoy, and enjoy the view. 🙏

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Stay safe, and keep the snacks in the car where they belong, lol. Yalla 🏜️

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee after the safety talk, a perfect ritual. Thank you, Omar.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dune safety and a dessert after. That's a balanced desert plan, I think.

posts.author: p06
posts.text: Stargazing spot recommendation: a quiet area past the Hatta dam with almost no light pollution. Bring a blanket, a red torch and a lot of patience for your eyes to adjust.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Stars past Hatta are incredible. The Milky Way is clearly visible in the winter months.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Red torch is the best tip, the bright white light ruins the night vision in seconds.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Lie on the sand with a blanket and watch the sky. The quiet is the best part.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee on a blanket under the stars, the best night in the desert. Thanks Kwame.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A snack and a blanket and the stars, my kind of Friday night. Dessert optional, very optional.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would bark at every shooting star, so I'll leave him at home for the stargazing.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Stargazing apps help identify constellations. Download the star map before you go.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: A star chart on paper plus a red torch, the old-fashioned way is the best way.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: We're planning a team stargazing night. Thanks for the spot, Kwame.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: @hannah_b enjoy it, the stars are amazing. Keep the group quiet for the best view.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Watch out for the cold after midnight. Layers and a flask of tea are my tip.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Night air in the desert is surprisingly chilly. Bring a warm hat too.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Respect the dark and the animals, keep the lights off the road when driving home.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll bring a thermos of hot coffee for the stargazing. Cold nights need hot drinks.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Hot chocolate for the stargazers, my treat. The stars and the sweets, the perfect night.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will be asleep by eight, so I'll send him a star photo instead. He'd approve.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A stargazing night is the best way to reset the week. Thank you for the tip, Kwame.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Stargazing with friends, a perfect Thursday night, and then a sleep in on Friday.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's make the stargazing night a monthly ritual for the team. Who's in?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Monthly stargazing, a brilliant habit. I'll bring the telescope if it fits in the car.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Telescope on the sand, a dream of a night. Good luck with the planning, Hannah.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Stay safe, keep the group close, and enjoy the stars. Yalla, Friday night.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Thanks, Kwame, the stars are calling us all. Coffee is ready, see you under the sky ✨

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Stars, cake and friends, what a lovely way to end the week. Thank you all.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Kwame, did you go on a clear night? The moon ruins the view for a few days.

posts.author: p08
posts.text: Honest desert picnic review: a shaded spot near the dam, a thermos of cold brew, dates and a small cheese board. Simple, cheap, and the best view for under 100 AED.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Dates and cheese in the desert is a lovely combo. Under 100 AED is a great achievement.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Cold brew on the dam side, the best picnic in the mountains. Thank you, Yusuf.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Simple picnics are the best. Good food, good company, good view, nothing else needed.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Shaded spot near the dam is hard to find in summer. Thanks for the tip, Yusuf.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Dates are my running snack too. Perfect for the mountain trail after a run.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy would eat the cheese board. Keep it out of his reach, please.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: A cold drink at the dam is the best reward after a hike. Swim later if allowed.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Under 100 AED for a view like that is a steal. Honest review, five stars.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our team picnic will copy this idea. Cheese board, dates, cold brew, perfect.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: @hannah_b copy away, the best ideas are shared. Enjoy the dam view.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Dam views are the best reason to drive the mountain road. Good food is the bonus.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Adding a small cake to the picnic next time, Yusuf. Dates and cake are a good pair.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Keep the rubbish in a bag and take it home. The dam area is beautiful, let's keep it so.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Leave no trace, always. Good reminder, friends, and nice picnic, Yusuf.

comments.author: p02
comments.text: A calm picnic after a run is my dream. Thanks for sharing the spot.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy approves of the picnic plan, as long as there is a bowl of water for him.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Water bowls and shade, the two essentials for pets and people in the mountains.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Picnic at the dam with friends, I'm sold. Yusuf, you are the picnic hero.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Let's plan the team picnic for next month, with the dates and the cold brew.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good plan. I'll bring my bike for the ride to the dam, the mountain road is lovely.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Yalla, picnic season is coming. Dates, cake, coffee, friends 🌴

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Thank you for the review, Yusuf. Honest reviews are my favourite kind.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Thanks, everyone. The dam is waiting, and the cold brew is cold. See you there ☕

comments.author: p02
comments.text: Reaching the dam at sunrise is the way to go for the cooler picnic, I suspect.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Cold brew in a flask keeps for hours, a clever trick for the mountain picnic.

posts.author: p02
posts.text: Monthly desert clean-up drive: meet at the lay-by, bring gloves and bags, collect rubbish along the dune edge and the roadside. Two hours, then a picnic. Who's joining?

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Clean-up drives are important. I'll bring the gloves and the big bags from the bike shop.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Count me in. A clean desert is a happy desert, and the picnic after is a bonus.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: I'll bring coffee for the crew. Clean-up and coffee, the perfect Saturday morning.

comments.author: p06
comments.text: Gloves and bags, I'm in. The playlist will keep the team going, low volume.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Picnic after the clean-up, I'll bring pastries and a sweet tea for the team.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy will not join the clean-up, but he'll supervise from the car with a water bowl.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Count me in too, Ravi. Our team will bring the bags and the energy.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Two hours is a good length. Bring hats, sunscreen, and plenty of water.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: Our office team wants to join too. How many people can the lay-by fit?

comments.author: p02
comments.text: @hannah_b the lay-by fits about ten cars. Carpool if you can, it's better for the planet.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Carpool is a great idea. I'll share the car list in the group this week.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: Keep the litter away from the sand edges, the wildlife can be affected by plastic.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Good point. Please bring a small bag for glass and a bigger one for general rubbish.

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Sorting the bags is a great idea, I'll bring the labels and a marker.

comments.author: p05
comments.text: Puppy's contribution: he will find the one lost glove, it's his special talent.

comments.author: p01
comments.text: A treasure hunt for gloves, I love it. Clean-up with a little fun, well done Ravi.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Please remember the heat, start early and take breaks in the shade. Safety first.

comments.author: p09
comments.text: We'll be there at 6:30 with the team. Thanks for organising, Ravi.

comments.author: p04
comments.text: Good, a team of volunteers makes the desert better, one bag at a time.

comments.author: p10
comments.text: The best way to give back to the desert, friends. See you at the lay-by.

comments.author: p08
comments.text: Coffee for everyone at the end, I've got the big thermos ready. Yalla, clean desert!

comments.author: p03
comments.text: A clean desert with a picnic after, the best Saturday ever. Thank you, Ravi 🏜️

comments.author: p01
comments.text: Gloves on, music low, bags full. See you all at the lay-by on Saturday.

comments.author: p07
comments.text: Thanks for the drive, friends. Let's leave the desert cleaner than we found it 🌵

comments.author: p03
comments.text: Count me in for the clean-up. Cake for the volunteers, obviously.
